brief: Tonight is Pull B, and it is your first session in eight days. I am not going to guess why you stopped, because the log does not say. What the log does say is that the last four times you wrote anything in it, you were arguing with the card: 'You're insane to have so many of the same corrective exercise back to back' on 28 July, 'Why four sets' and 'What the fuck..why did you put this in terms of seconds' on 30 July, 'Do you have a brain?' on 31 July, and 'Are the trainers sure three sets is correct?' on 2 August. Then five straight training days, and then silence. Those may be two unrelated facts. I am not treating them as one. But I am not going to open with your bent-over row and pretend the other thing is not sitting there. There are four cards waiting for you on the plan screen and three of them are the answers to those exact complaints: the straight-arm pulldown rep range that made the weight impossible to move, the Push A pushdown range you have never once finished, and the Legs A calf sets down from four to the three you actually do. The fourth takes face pulls off Push A entirely and puts the reverse pec deck there instead. That is the last place face pulls are still in your week, and you have now told me in writing twice that you do not want them. Tap through those four and the program stops asking you for things you have already refused. Now tonight. The row repeats exactly what you did on 28 July: 115, 135, 145, then 150. The top set asks for 9, which is the same 9 you already own, not the 10 you missed. Two weeks off this lift is not the night to chase a rep you have never hit on a cold hinge, and the 10 will be there next time. Close-grip pulldown is the one thing going up: 127.5 for 8 on all three sets. You took 120 for a clean 10, 10, 10 last time, which is the top of that range on every set, so the raise is earned outright — and 127.5 is not new ground, you pulled it for three sets on four separate nights in January and February. Eight reps instead of ten is where the time off gets paid back. Cable reverse curl comes down to 35 for three sets of 12. At 37.5 your reps ran 12, 11, 10 and this slot asks for at least 12, so the weight was wrong, not you. It is also the last lift of the night, and the last lift is the one you have been quietly dropping — two sets instead of three on 31 July, two on 3 August. It is three short sets. Finish it. The rest hold: straight-arm pulldown 37.5 for 13 across, shrugs 70 for 14 across, incline curls 25s for 10, 10, 10 — that third set is the whole job, you got 9 last time. Rest three minutes on the row, about 75 seconds after that. One more thing, and it matters more than any number here. You have one bodyweight reading since 4 January — 206 lb on 21 July — and one cardio session in the entire log. You are about twenty-nine weeks out. Standing on a scale this morning is worth more to March than anything on tonight's card.

flags.note: Nothing logged from 4 to 10 August — eight days, the longest break in this block. Tonight's numbers are built on your 3 August data, because that is the last thing this review can see.
No review ran on 8, 9 or 10 August — the automatic morning job did not fire. Until this morning your app was showing you the review from 7 August. Today's is fresh.

Your bent-over row numbers have changed three times since you last trained, with no new session logged to justify any of it. Tonight's card puts them back to exactly what you did on 28 July and they will not move again until you log a session.

The last four notes you wrote were objections to the prescription, and then the log goes quiet for eight days. Nothing in it says those are connected, and I am not assuming they are — but the four cards waiting on your plan screen are the fixes to three of those four complaints.
One bodyweight reading since 4 January (206 lb on 21 July) and one cardio session in the whole log. At roughly twenty-nine weeks out, that is the thinnest part of your prep.

Monday 3 August's Arnold presses are still not counted — you swapped them for the Smith overhead press and the slot stored zero sets, so that work cannot move the slot. Logging a substitute under the slot it replaces is what keeps it counting.

proposals.why: Still open from last week and it is on tonight's card: both your last two Pull B nights sat at 37.5 and finished 13, 11, 12 and 13, 12, 12 — never the fifteen this slot asks for, so the weight can never move, and asking ten to twelve means the twelves you already do earn the next step.

Still open from last week: Push A's rope pushdown asks ten to twelve and your six sets there came in at eight, seven, nine and eight, seven, eight — not one set inside the range all block, so the weight can never move, and twelve to fifteen makes it a slot you can actually finish.

Still open from last week, and this is not the cut to two sets you declined on 3 August — it is three: Legs A asks for four and you have done two, two and three, and because the weight only moves when you finish every set the plan asks for, three makes the prescription the work you actually do.

Push A is the last place face pulls are still in your week, and it is the one prescription you have objected to in writing twice — 'I did angels and demons instead' on 28 July and 'Do you have a brain?' on 31 July — so this puts the reverse pec deck there instead, same back of the shoulder, on the machine you have carried from 82.5 to 90 without missing a set.

dissent.progression: Repeat the four weights but ask for 10 on the top set — it is the one rep still owed before the load can move.
dissent.recovery: Repeat 28 July exactly, top set at the 9 he already owns; fourteen days since the last Pull B and this is a cold hinge-loaded row done first.
dissent.why: Recovery wins on the rep because the fact that changed since the last review is time, not performance: on 7 August this was a four-day gap and today it is eight, with fourteen days since he last rowed. Asking for a rep he has never hit, on the heaviest hinged set of the night, on a re-entry session, risks a miss recorded on his first card back for the sake of one rep that will still be there next Pull B. I am also holding these four weights still for a second reason: this lift has been prescribed three different ways since he last trained, with no new session logged to justify any of it, and the churn stops here.

dissent.progression: Raise to 127.5 for 8 across — 120 for 10, 10, 10 is the top of the range on every set, so the step is earned.
dissent.recovery: Stay at 120 on the grounds that he has not topped the range at this weight yet.
dissent.why: Recovery's premise is contradicted by the log. This slot asks eight to ten, and on 28 July he finished 120 for exactly ten on all three sets — that is the top of the range, not short of it, so the raise is earned rather than speculative. It is also not new territory: he pulled 127.5 for three sets on four separate nights in January and February. Recovery's real concern is the size of the step, and the reps answer it — eight is the bottom of the range, which is where the eight days off get paid back.

dissent.progression: Drop to 35 and keep three sets — at 37.5 he ran 12, 11, 10 and two of three sets finished under the twelve-rep floor.
dissent.recovery: Keep 37.5 but cut to two sets, because this is now the closing lift and he has been truncating closing lifts.
dissent.why: Both seats are right about a different problem and only one of them is fixable with a number. The weight is the cause: at 37.5 the prescription cannot be completed as written, which is the same deadlock that has frozen three other lifts in this block all month. Cutting to two sets at a weight he still cannot finish hides that instead of fixing it. Recovery's point about the closing lift is real and evidenced, so it is answered in the brief rather than in the load — the card asks for three short sets at a weight that allows twelve, and the brief tells him plainly to finish it.

overrides.reason: Exactly what you did on 28 July. The top set asks for the 9 you already own, not the 10 you missed — two weeks off this lift is not the night to chase a new rep on a cold hinge.

You took 120 for a clean 10, 10, 10 last time, the top of the range on every set, so this step is earned — and you pulled 127.5 for three sets on four nights back in January and February. Eight reps is where the time off gets paid back.
Same weight, one more rep than you finished on. You got 13, 12, 12 last time; the next weight up on this machine is 45, which is far too big a jump from here.
Same 70s, one more rep on the last two sets than last time. The next dumbbells are the 80s with nothing in between, so reps are the only currency here.
Stay on the 25s — the rack jumps straight to 30. The third set is the whole job: you got 9 last time and 8 the time before.
Down to 35. At 37.5 your reps ran 12, 11, 10 and this slot asks for at least 12, so the weight was wrong, not your effort. It is the last lift of the night and it is three short sets — finish it.
